articles.summary: Key Takeaways Thin hair and thinning hair are different. Thinning hair refers to a reduction in hair density over time, while thin hair is often determined by genetics. The right haircut can create the appearance of more volume. Layers, bobs, pixie cuts, and strategic shaping help build movement and dimension. Hair density influences how full hair appears. Volume is often determined by both the number of hairs on the scalp and the way hair is cut and styled. Lightweight products help support volume. Volumizing shampoos, conditioners, leave-ins, and styling products can help prevent hair from becoming weighed down. Scalp health and hair care habits matter. Heat styling, tight hairstyles, product buildup, and environmental stressors can influence how hair looks and behaves over time.

articles.summary: Switching up your hair color is always an exciting event, especially when you’re entering into a new season of your life. If you ask us, no change is more transformative to your overall look than your hair color. A new hue makes a bold statement about who you are and what you want to become. But committing to a new color can be intimidating. Where do you even begin in your search for the perfect hue? If you’re in need of hair color ideas that complement your complexion and style, we’ve got you. From mega-dramatic tones that give you a whole new look to low-maintenance colors that suit your busy lifestyle, this guide offers hair color ideas that will work for you. Concerned about compromising the health of your hair? We’re also here to offer tips on maintaining your color and keeping your locks in prime condition. Best Hair Color Ideas: 6 Fabulous Options to Consider We firmly believe that any color can work for any person. If you want bright pink hair with blue highlights in a pixie cut, go for it! But there are some guidelines to help you choose the best hair color idea for your complexion ⁠— let’s explain. Most hair colors either lean towards warm or cool tones. The same goes for your skin tone. If you have yellow, gold, or peachy undertones, you have a warm complexion. If you have blue or pink undertones, your complexion is cool. Not sure which one describes you? Here’s a quick trick: Examine the color of the veins on your wrist to determine the type of complexion you have. Blue veins mean you have cool undertones and green veins mean you have warm undertones. For your hair and skin tone to complement each other, select a hair color that’s within your warm or cool color family. Let’s review six on-trend hair color ideas to see which ones might work for you. Chocolate Brown Chocolate brown is one of the richest, most beautiful hair shades out there. It looks amazing on those with warm golden skin tones and can bring out any eye color. Since this is such a dimensional shade, we’d only suggest it for those with a lot of time to commit to the chocolatey aesthetic. If your natural hair color is much lighter or darker than chocolate, you’ll need frequent touch-ups to maintain this rich hue. Pro Tip: Check out more brown hair color ideas. Bronde There’s a fine line between dirty blonde and light brown hair and it’s called bronde. This color blends blonde and brown tones to give you a trendy, low-maintenance look. Being “bronde” can truly work for everybody, so long as you choose the right shade for you. If you have naturally dark hair and are looking to go bronde, we’d first recommend getting darker blonde highlights. Choosing golden blonde or caramel highlights will give you a bronde look you can easily maintain when your dark roots grow out. For blondes wanting to go darker, ask your colorist for lowlights in brunette shades like mushroom or light golden brown. Gray The gray hair color trend can look modern, playful, and sophisticated all at the same time. Gray shades work best on those with cool undertones. If you’re looking to layer a gray tone over your current color, choose a shade close to your natural hue. If you have naturally lighter hair, go with a light lavender or silvery blonde hue. If your hair is naturally dark, a charcoal or blue-gray shade will flatter your tresses. Pro Tip: Explore more gray hair color ideas. Black Give your hairstyle the ultimate edge by dying it the darkest shade of all. Black hair is undeniably mysterious and dramatic, especially if you’ve been rocking lighter tresses for some time. If you’re not sure if this raven-toned hair color idea is for you, here are some things to consider. Paler complexions with cool undertones will find black hair to be more flattering than those with peachy, warm undertones who may find that this dark shade washes them out. If you have a medium to darker skin tone, your richer pigment allows you to pull off this dramatic shade well. If your complexion is rich in golden or yellow undertones, mix in mocha brown balayage highlights to add multidimensional warm tones to your tresses. Rose Gold The pastel hair trend is still having a moment, but this time it’s veering into natural tones with redhead-adjacent shades of rose gold. This color looks kind of like strawberry blonde but has more pinky elements to it, making it best for those with warm, golden, or peach undertones. If you want to experiment with this cotton candy shade, layer a rose gold ombre hair color over your locks or add some peekaboo hair highlights to the ends of your tresses. Pro Tip: Got redhead curiosity? Check out more red hair color ideas. Platinum Blonde Platinum blonde is an iconic shade that many desire but few have the guts to commit to. If you love this Barbie-like blonde hair color idea but are afraid you can’t pull it off, think again. Platinum naturally complements those with pale skin and light eyes, but having these features isn’t required to rock this cool blonde shade. If your skin has cool undertones (and you’re ready for all the attention this color is going to give you), go platinum! The biggest question and concern about going platinum is whether bleaching it will destroy one’s hair. The answer is yes ⁠— unless you take the right steps to prevent major damage. The bleaching process is toughest on black or brunette hair because the darker your natural hair color is, the more rounds of bleach you’ll have to go through to get it to platinum. So if you’re dead set on taking your dark hair to the lightest of light shades, you have to commit to routine TLC for your tresses. Pro Tip: Try a purple shampoo to preserve platinum color and combat brassy tones. How to Care for Color-Treated Hair The downside of committing to a new hair color is that it can come with some degree of hair damage. Hair dye works by penetrating hair cuticles to deposit or remove color in the cortex, causing swelling and some damage to the hair strands. Regular dye jobs can cause your hair to feel rough, dry, tangled, and frizzy. Luckily, using a hair mask can make your hair look and feel a lot better. Function of Beauty’s customized hair mask is made to help replenish color damaged hair. It’s created with conditioning agents like argan oil, Japanese sake, and jojoba ester oil to give you more hydration than a traditional conditioner. Coat your strands with this product once or twice a week to improve softness and help restore the moisture your tresses need. Now That You’ve Found the Best Hair Color Idea ... With so many hair color ideas, it can be daunting to choose one. But once you know how to choose a hair tone that works with your complexion ⁠— and understand how much time it takes to keep up with color commitments ⁠— it’ll be much easier to decide on a perfect hue. To help maintain your new hair color, Function of Beauty has you covered. Take this hair quiz to build a custom shampoo and conditioner combo. This hair washing set can be optimized with goals such as color protection, which will prevent fading and enhance your strands for optimum color uptake and long lasting color.
articles.title: 6 Hair Color Ideas to Compliment You

Hair's ability to absorb and retain moisture plays a major role in dryness, frizz, and product performance. Scalp health influences hair health. Oil production, moisture balance, and scalp condition help shape how your hair looks and feels. The best routine is personalized. Understanding your hair's unique architecture helps you choose products and techniques that support healthier-looking hair.

articles.summary: Disclaimer: The information provided is not intended as medical advice. For any medical concerns, always contact your doctor or dermatologist.When it comes to healthy hair, what you put on your plate matters just as much as the products you apply to your strands. After all, the scalp is home to around 100,000 hair follicles, and each one relies on a steady supply of nutrients to function at its best. While there’s no single vitamin guaranteed to give you longer, thicker hair overnight, a balanced diet can help support healthy hair growth, strength, and shine.It's also worth noting that more isn't always better. Experts agree that vitamins and supplements shouldn't replace a nutritious diet, and taking high doses of certain nutrients may do more harm than good. If you're concerned that you may not be getting enough of a particular nutrient, don't self-diagnose based on internet searches alone. Nutrient deficiencies should be confirmed through proper medical evaluation and testing. Before adding supplements to your routine, talk with your doctor or dermatologist to determine whether a deficiency is actually present and what treatment approach is right for you. 11 Nutrients and Vitamins for Hair 11 Nutrients and Vitamins for Healthy HairHealthy hair looks different for everyone, whether you have sleek straight strands, voluminous curls, or textured coils. But regardless of your hair type, strong, resilient strands start with proper nourishment. 2. Vitamin A Vitamin A supports normal cell growth throughout the body, including the cells that make up your hair and scalp. Foods rich in vitamin A include: Sweet potatoes, carrots, spinach, kale, butternut squash, cantaloupe, and eggs. 2. Vitamin B2 (Riboflavin) Riboflavin helps convert food into energy and supports normal cellular function. Because healthy hair growth requires a constant supply of energy, this B vitamin plays a supporting role in maintaining healthy strands. Foods rich in riboflavin include: Milk, yogurt, eggs, salmon, lean beef, mushrooms, almonds, spinach. 3. Vitamin B7 (Biotin) Biotin has become one of the most talked-about nutrients for hair health, but if you aren’t deficient, it won’t help much. It’s involved in the production of keratin, the protein that makes up hair, skin and nails. Foods rich in biotin include: Eggs, salmon, avocados, sweet potatoes, sunflower seeds, almonds, beef liver. 4. Vitamin B9 (Folate or Folic Acid) Folate helps support healthy cell growth and renewal, making it an important nutrient for tissues throughout the body—including the scalp. Foods rich in folate include: Lentils, chickpeas, black beans, spinach, asparagus, Brussels sprouts, and avocados. 5. Vitamin C Vitamin C is an antioxidant that helps protect cells from oxidative stress. It also supports collagen production, a structural protein found throughout the body. Foods rich in vitamin C include: Oranges, grapefruit, strawberries, kiwi, bell peppers, broccoli, and Brussels sprouts. 6. Vitamin D Vitamin D plays a role in many bodily functions, including supporting healthy skin and scalp health. While sunlight helps your body produce vitamin D naturally, certain foods can help you meet your daily needs as well. Sources of vitamin D include: Salmon, sardines, egg yolks, fortified milk, fortified cereals, and UV-exposed mushrooms. 7. Vitamin E As an antioxidant, vitamin E helps protect cells from oxidative damage and supports overall skin and scalp health. Foods rich in vitamin E include: Almonds, sunflower seeds, hazelnuts, peanuts, avocados, spinach, and olive oil. 8. Protein and Collagen-Supporting Nutrients Hair is primarily made of keratin, a protein. That’s why consuming enough protein is one ef the most important dietary habits for maintaining healthy hair. Protein-rich foods include: Chicken, turkey, fish, eggs, Greek yogurt, lentils, tofu, and tempeh.For additional collagen support, pair protein-rich foods with vitamin C-rich fruits and vegetables. 9. Omega-3 Fatty Acids Omega-3 fatty acids help support scalp health and contribute to overall skin hydration. Since the body cannot product them on its own, they need to come from food. Foods rich in omega-3s include: Salmon, mackerel, sardines, herring, chia seeds, flaxseeds, walnuts. 10. Iron Iron helps transport oxygen throughout the body, including the the tissues that support healthy hair growth. Foods rich in iron include: Lean red meat, oysters, lentils, beans, spinach, pumpkin seeds, fortified cereals 11. Selenium Selenium supports several important functions in the body, including healthy thyroid function and antioxidant activity. Foods rich in selenium include: Brazil nuts, tuna, sardines, shrimp, eggs, brown rice, and whole grains. That’s where Function of Beauty’s 100% custom-made formulations come in handy. articles.summary: Key Takeaways Not all hair oils work the same way. Different oils vary in weight, absorption, and how they support moisture retention and hair manageability. Hair oils help support the cuticle. A smoother cuticle can improve shine, reduce friction, and help minimize frizz and breakage. Hair type influences which oil works best. Thick, coarse, curly, and coily hair often benefit from richer oils, while fine or oily hair may prefer lightweight options. Oils support moisture retention, but they don't add water to the hair. Their primary role is helping seal and protect moisture already present in the hair fiber. The best hair oil is the one suited to your hair's structure and needs. Personalized routines help ensure your products support your unique hair type, environment, and goals.

articles.summary: Key Takeaways Hair damage occurs when the protective cuticle layer becomes compromised by heat, friction, chemical treatments, environmental exposure, or harsh grooming habits. Common signs of damaged hair include dryness, frizz, dullness, split ends, breakage, rough texture, and increased tangling. Gentle hair care habits, including careful detangling and reducing unnecessary friction, can help minimize future damage. Heat styling, chemical processing, chlorine, salt water, and excessive brushing can all contribute to weakening the hair fiber over time. Hydration is essential for maintaining healthy-looking hair and helping improve softness, smoothness, and manageability. Deep conditioning treatments, leave-in conditioners, and heat protectants can help support the hair's moisture balance and protective barrier.
